options.description: You can skip the questions. The letter then gets a neutral opening with the gap noted, and no enthusiasm is invented. Forbidden-letter cases still ask nothing. This is what the change already does, so I would keep it.
options.label: Allow an explicit skip

options.description: Every letter waits for your answers to the three questions. There is no skip path and no neutral opening. A letter the employer forbids is not drafted, so no questions are asked for it. Recommended: your words say 'always', so this is the closest to them.
options.label: Always ask, no skip (Recommended)

payload.question: You said the cover letter workflow should always clarify why a company, your other motivations and what you want to put forward. Should it ever go ahead without your answers, either because you choose to skip the questions or because the employer forbids a letter?
